Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.

Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.
Under guidance, participates in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers.

1. Decision making: Evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems.

Prepares special data releases, reviews and verifies data sources and methods of data compilation; develops and implements procedures for the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data.
Develops and outlines new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions.
Reviews and designs questionnaires for the collection of data and assesses the timeliness, completeness, accuracy and validity of data compiled for publication.
Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to collect, process, edit, compile and present statistical data.
Develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches to improve existing surveys or to meet specific needs.
2. Leadership and operational management: Participates in project teams, work groups, meetings and conferences in order to develop and improve work methods and practices, share knowledge and contribute to skill development.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communiction: Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.

Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
Knowledge of current and emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series.
Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey is required in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques.
Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects.

Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data.
Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.
Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.
Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.
